sources.citation: Wega Simeu, Abraham. 2004. Etude phonologique du pólrí. Mémoire (maîtrise), Université de Yaoundé I. iii+124 pp. (Language Description Heritage digital copy, MPG PuRe item_403563; Glottolog ref 100791)
sources.note: Chapter I 'Les tons' (printed pp. 7-11): defines tone after Wiesemann et al. 1983, states pólrì is a tone language, inventories high, low, rising, falling tones, proves each distinctive by minimal pairs and concludes there are four tonemes (H, L level; LH, HL contour). Ch. II.1 gives tone distributions by word length (a word never carries two contour tones). No mention of accent or stress anywhere (full-text search 'accent' = 0 hits).

sources.citation: Ballif, Noël. 1955. Dancer of God. London: Sidgwick and Jackson (English translation of Les Danseurs de Dieu: chez les Pygmées de la Sangha, Paris: Hachette, 1954). archive.org item dli.ernet.524336 (Digital Library of India).
sources.note: No phonology content. pp. 142-144: 'Having taken down the first words of the Pomo vocabulary I was compiling on behalf of the Institute of Ethnology, I next asked Alexandre to dictate to me some of the proverbs of the Pomo. I wrote them phonetically, noting the translation word for word.' p. 175: finishing 'a typical vocabulary of the Pomo and the Lingala'; Lingala used as lingua franca between Pomo and Babenzélé. Full-text search for tone/tonal/accent/pitch/syllable finds nothing about the language.

sources.citation: Bruel, Georges. 1911. Notes ethnographiques sur quelques tribus de l'Afrique équatoriale française. Fasc. I: Les populations de la Moyenne-Sanga: Pomo, Boumali, Babinga. Paris: Ernest Leroux. (reprint of Revue d'ethnographie et de sociologie 1, 1910, 3-32 and 111-126)
sources.note: Ethnography with an 'Appendice' (book p. 39ff., pp. 67-72) headed 'Vocabulaire Pomo': a bare French-Pomo/Boumali/Lino/Ndzimou wordlist in French orthography, introduced by one sentence ('nous donnons ci-dessous quelques éléments de vocabulaires que nous avons pu recueillir'). No remark on accent, tone, syllables or pronunciation anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent/tonique/prononc/ton/syllab; page 39 checked visually). Silent on stress.

sources.note: Concerns Babinga/Mbakka pygmy vocabularies of the Kadéï and Sangha, not Pomo; mentions 'les Mpomo de la Ndoki' only as a neighbouring Fang-related tribe; cites Bruel 1910. Nothing on Pomo stress.
